intro.title: MineSweeper Project Overview
intro.desc: This page presents the architecture of my MineSweeper project, including core gameplay logic, scene flow design, and implementation details through code and runtime demonstrations.

summary.text: The MineSweeper project is implemented in C++ with a modular structure based on a main loop, scene classes, and a scene manager. The code blocks below highlight the core control flow and responsibilities of each module. The videos demonstrate gameplay transitions, reveal rules, and boundary handling behavior in practice.

game_mode.title: Game Mode Demo
game_mode.desc: Shows mode selection and primary interaction flow.

main_flow.title: Main Gameplay Flow
main_flow.desc: Shows the end-to-end transition from launch to active gameplay.

safe_cell.title: Safe Cell Expansion
safe_cell.desc: Shows automatic expansion behavior for empty connected regions.

safe_zone.title: Safe Zone Validation
safe_zone.desc: Shows zone search logic and boundary condition handling.

main_loop.title: Main Loop
main_loop.desc: Controls input handling, update steps, rendering, and exit conditions.

scene_class.title: Scene Class
scene_class.desc: Defines scene behavior, board state interfaces, and game-state transitions.

scene_manager.title: Scene Manager
scene_manager.desc: Handles scene registration, switching, and lifecycle management.

board.title: Board Module
board.desc: Defines board data, mine placement, and cell-level state operations.
